Below is a gentle, progressive 12‑week postpartum return program designed for a 33‑year‑old, four weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It respects current restrictions (light activity only; walking; no direct “abs” work, heavy lifting, or impact until six‑week check) and then gradually advances contingent on OB clearance at six weeks. Emphasis is on breathing, pelvic floor and deep core re‑engagement, posture, circulation, mobility, and gradual load tolerance. All sessions are low equipment (yoga mat) and organized week‑by‑week with clear progressions. Monitor for red flags (see Safety Notes at end).

Structure
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 4–5 postpartum): Restorative recovery, breath/pelvic floor reconnection, walking tolerance, gentle mobility. No direct abdominal loading, no planks/sit-ups, no heavy lifting, no impact.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 6–8): After 6‑week OB clearance to progress, begin foundational strength, progressive walking, gentle core reconditioning (deep core only), introduce controlled tempo and isometrics.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Incremental strengthening, increased work capacity, intro to low‑impact dynamic patterns if asymptomatic, maintain core/pelvic floor focus.

Session Format (general)
- Frequency:
  - Weeks 4–5: 3 movement sessions/week + walking most days.
  - Weeks 6–8: 3–4 sessions/week + walking most days.
  - Weeks 9–12: 4 sessions/week + walking most days.
- Session length: 15–35 minutes initially, building to 30–45 minutes by Weeks 9–12.
- Each session:
  1) Breath and pelvic floor connection (5–8 min)
  2) Mobility/activation (5–8 min)
  3) Main set (strength/control; 10–25 min)
  4) Cool‑down, downregulation breathing (3–5 min)
- Intensity: Aim RPE 3–4/10 early, progressing to 5–6/10 by Weeks 9–12. No breath‑holding or bearing down (Valsalva).

Key Techniques
- 360 breathing: Inhale through nose, expand ribcage laterally/back; allow pelvic floor to relax. Exhale through pursed lips, gently draw pelvic floor upward (like lifting a blueberry) and engage deep abdominals (think “hug baby” or “zip up” below navel) at low intensity (20–30% effort).
- Scar care: Only if OB cleared and incision fully closed—gentle desensitization around, not on, scar; no aggressive massage in this plan.
- Alignment cues: Ribs stacked over pelvis, neutral spine, soft knees, relaxed shoulders, avoid doming/coning along midline.

Contraindications/Modify/Stop if
- Increased vaginal bleeding, new or worsening pelvic pain, heaviness/pressure/bulge (prolapse signs), urinary/fecal leakage, wound pain/redness, fever, calf pain/swelling, dizziness, sharp abdominal pain, visible coning or doming during exercises. Regress or pause and consult provider.

WEEK‑BY‑WEEK PLAN

Weeks 4–5 postpartum (Phase 1: Restore and Reconnect)
Goal: Establish daily breath/pelvic floor coordination, gentle mobility, circulation, and walking tolerance without symptoms.

Walking (most days)
- Start 10–20 minutes at comfortable pace, flat terrain. Break into 5–10 min chunks if needed. Add 5 minutes every few days as tolerated up to 25–30 min by end of Week 5. Maintain conversational pace; no hills or brisk intervals yet.

Session A (3x/week)
1) Breath/PF (5–6 min)
- 360 Breathing with PF relaxation on inhale, gentle lift on exhale: 6–8 breaths x 2–3 sets (positions: side‑lying with pillow, hook‑lying).
- Exhale‑based core setting: On exhale, gently “zip” lower abdomen for 3–4 seconds; relax fully on inhale. 6–8 reps.

2) Mobility/Activation (6–8 min)
- Neck/shoulder rolls: 5 each way.
- Cat‑cow (very small range): 6–8 reps, pain‑free.
- Seated/standing thoracic rotations: 6/side.
- Ankle pumps/circles: 10/side.
- Pelvic clocks (supine, minimal motion): 5–8 each direction.

3) Main Set (10–12 min)
- Sit‑to‑stand to high chair/bench: 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps, slow, exhale on up.
- Heel slides (supine), exhale as heel slides out; maintain flat-ish abdomen (no doming): 2 sets x 6–8/side.
- Glute bridge (mini range, no rib flare): 2 sets x 6–8, 3‑second exhale on lift.
- Standing wall scapular slides: 2 sets x 8–10.

4) Cool‑Down
- 2–3 minutes downregulation breathing in supported position.

Session B (Optional light day or swap; 1–2x/week)
- Gentle walk + 10 minutes of mobility: child’s pose (supported), side‑lying open books, calf stretch, chest doorway stretch (gentle), all 20–30 seconds x 2.

Week 5 progression notes
- Nudge reps to 8–10, add a third set only if zero symptoms and good form.
- Introduce side‑lying clamshells (light band only after Week 6; for now, bodyweight): 2 sets x 8–10/side.
- Add marching bridge (alternating heel lift only, pelvis steady): 2 sets x 6/side if regular bridge is symptom‑free.

Week 6 (Phase 2 begins only after OB clearance to progress)
Goal: Maintain walking; begin foundational strength and gentle deep core reconditioning. Still avoid high intra‑abdominal pressure, heavy lifting, impact, long planks/sit‑ups/crunches.

Walking
- 25–35 minutes most days. Introduce 2 x 2‑minute slightly brisk intervals separated by 3 minutes easy if symptom‑free.

Sessions (3–4/week; alternate A and B)

Session A
1) Breath/PF (6 min)
- 360 breathing with 3–4 second exhale holds, 6–8 breaths x 2 sets.
- Supine pelvic floor lifts: 6–8 reps with full rest between.

2) Mobility/Activation (6–8 min)
- Cat‑cow small range: 8–10.
- Quadruped rocking: 8–10.
- Thoracic open books: 6–8/side.

3) Main Set (20–25 min)
Circuit x 2–3 rounds, 60–75 sec rest between exercises as needed:
- Sit‑to‑stand (arms forward counterbalance): 10–12.
- Elevated incline push‑up at wall or countertop: 8–10, exhale on push.
- Quadruped limb reach (bird‑dog arms only or legs only initially): 6–8/side, pause 2s, no trunk shift.
- Bridge: 10–12 with 2–3s hold at top.
- Standing band pull‑apart (if band available; if not, wall scap slides): 10–12.

4) Cool‑Down
- Supine breathing, gentle hip flexor stretch at edge of bed, 20–30s x 2/side.

Session B
1) Breath/PF (6 min)
- 360 breathing + gentle PF lifts in seated and standing: 6–8 reps each.

2) Mobility/Activation
- Lateral hip shifts against wall, 6–8/side.
- Ankle/knee/hip controlled ranges, 5–6 each.

3) Main Set
- Reverse lunge to knee tap (assisted, hold chair) or split‑stance sit‑to‑stand: 6–8/side.
- Dead bug pattern (alternating heel taps only; arms to ceiling): 6–8/side; exhale on tap; stop if any coning.
- Side‑lying clamshells: 10–12/side.
- Standing overhead reach to calf raise: 8–10, slow.

4) Cool‑Down
- Child’s pose (supported), thoracic rotations, neck stretches.

Week 7 progression
- Add one round to circuits if RPE ≤5 and symptom‑free.
- Bird‑dog: progress to opposite arm/leg if stable.
- Bridges: add isometric hold 5 seconds x 8–10 reps.
- Incline push‑ups slightly lower surface if easy, maintain zero doming and no breath‑hold.

Week 8 progression
- Introduce hip hinge pattern with dowel/broom for patterning: 2–3 sets x 8–10 (no load; focus on ribs over pelvis).
- Step‑ups to low, stable step (4–6"): 2–3 sets x 8/side, use support as needed.
- Dead bug: progress to single‑leg extension with arms still, 6–8/side, only if no coning.

Weeks 9–10 (Phase 3: Build Capacity)
Goal: Increase strength endurance and functional tolerance. Still avoid high‑pressure moves if any coning/leakage. Low impact only unless fully symptom‑free.

Walking
- 30–45 minutes most days. Up to 3–4 x 2–3 minute brisk intervals separated by easy walking. Introduce small hills if symptom‑free.

Sessions (4/week; split into 2 Strength + 1 Core/Mobility + 1 Conditioning/Low‑Impact day)

Strength Day 1 (Lower focus)
1) Prep: Breath/PF + hip/ankle mobility (6–8 min).
2) Main (3 rounds)
- Squat to box or air squat: 10–12.
- Hip hinge with broomstick + mini pause at mid‑shin: 10.
- Step‑ups (6–8"): 8–10/side.
- Side‑lying clamshells or banded if available: 12–15/side.
- Calf raises: 12–15.
3) Accessory
- Marching bridge: 8–10/side.
4) Cool‑Down breathing and gentle hip flexor stretch.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + posterior chain)
1) Prep: Thoracic mobility and breath.
2) Main (3 rounds)
- Incline push‑up (countertop or sturdy table): 8–12.
- Quadruped row (isometric: press hand into floor while pulling opposite elbow toward hip without moving trunk) 8/side x 3s hold.
- Bird‑dog opposite arm/leg: 8/side with 2s pause.
- Wall slide to Y lift (if able): 10–12.
- Bridge with abduction (knees press gently out against hands): 10–12.
3) Cool‑Down.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing patterns: 2 sets x 6–8 breaths.
- Dead bug variations: heel taps or single‑leg extension depending on tolerance, 2–3 sets x 6–8/side.
- Side plank regression (elevated: forearm on couch, knees bent) 10–20s x 2/side if no coning or pelvic pressure; otherwise skip.
- Open books, cat‑cow small, thread‑the‑needle, gentle hamstring/calf/hip flexor stretches.

Conditioning/Low‑Impact Day
- Brisk walk intervals or stroller walk with posture focus: 25–35 min total.
- Optional circuit 2–3 rounds at easy‑moderate:
  - Sit‑to‑stand x 12
  - Step‑back lunge taps x 8/side
  - Incline push‑ups x 10
  - Calf raises x 15
  Rest as needed, keep breathing steady.

Progression checkpoints Weeks 9–10
- No leakage, heaviness, or coning with effort? If yes, maintain or progress slightly (more reps/tempo). If no, regress to previous successful variation.

Weeks 11–12 (Phase 3 continued: Strength and Function)
Goal: Consolidate strength, introduce gentle tempo, add unilateral control, prepare for return to broader fitness after 12+ weeks pending individual readiness.

Walking/Conditioning
- 35–50 minutes most days; intervals 4–5 x 3 minutes brisk, 2 minutes easy if desired and symptom‑free.

Sessions (4/week)

Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat to air squat with 2–3s down, 1s pause, drive up: 3 sets x 8–10.
- Hip hinge to mid‑shin with longer torso pause (3s): 3 x 8–10.
- Step‑ups (8–10"): 3 x 8–10/side, slow eccentric.
- Split‑squat to box (short range) holding onto support: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Calf raises single‑leg support‑assisted: 2–3 x 8–10/side.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push‑up lower surface if able: 3 x 8–12.
- Tall kneeling or half‑kneeling press‑outs with band if available; if none, isometric wall press (forearms into wall) 3 x 20–30s.
- Bird‑dog slow tempo 3s out/3s back: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Side plank (knees) 15–25s x 2–3/side if no symptoms.
- Bridge march or single‑leg bridge partial range: 3 x 6–8/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing: 2 sets.
- Dead bug progressed (arm and opposite leg reach) if zero doming: 2–3 x 6/side.
- Pallof press with band if available; if not, anti‑rotation hold (hands clasped, arms extended, resist trunk turn) 3 x 15–20s/side.
- Mobility flow: thoracic, hips, calves, chest.

Conditioning/Capacity Day
- Circuit x 3–4 rounds at RPE 5–6:
  - Sit‑to‑stand x 12–15
  - Step‑back lunge taps or split‑squat short range x 8–10/side
  - Incline push‑ups x 10–12
  - Hip hinge x 10–12
  - Calf raises x 15
  Rest 60–75s as needed, keep breath flowing.

General Coaching Cues Across Program
- Exhale on exertion; inhale on the easier phase.
- Keep engagement gentle (20–30% effort) for pelvic floor and deep core early; never strain.
- Watch midline for doming/coning; if present, modify by reducing range, load, or changing position.
- Posture during walks: ribs stacked over pelvis, slight lean into hills from ankles, not hips.

Recovery and Lifestyle
- Sleep: Prioritize naps and nighttime sleep when possible; training volume should flex with fatigue.
- Hydration: Aim ~2–3 L/day, more if breastfeeding and per OB advice.
- Nutrition: Emphasize protein ~1.2–1.6 g/kg/day, ample fiber, fruits/veg, and healthy fats. If breastfeeding, add ~300–500 kcal/day guided by hunger and provider advice. Micronutrients: continue prenatal/postnatal per OB.
- Bowel care: Fiber, fluids, walking, and avoid straining; exhale gently during bowel movements.
- Scar/Incision: Keep clean/dry; only gentle surrounding tissue movement once fully healed and cleared; avoid direct pressure early.
- Pelvic floor support: Consider brief use of high‑waist supportive garments for comfort (not tight binders). If any prolapse/heaviness symptoms, refer to pelvic health PT.

Red Flags/When to Refer
- Any increase in bleeding, wound issues, fever, chest pain, calf pain/swelling, persistent urinary/fecal incontinence, pelvic heaviness/pressure, or significant diastasis doming—pause exercise and consult OB. Consider referral to pelvic floor physical therapist anytime concerns arise.

Notes for the Trainer
- This plan assumes uncomplicated course and OB clearance to progress at 6 weeks. If clearance is delayed or symptoms appear, extend prior week’s programming until symptom‑free and cleared.
- Keep sessions adaptable—on low‑sleep days, perform only breath work, mobility, and a short walk.
- Document symptom response to each progression to individualize pace.

Here’s a practical breastfeeding‑supportive nutrition plan to layer onto the 12‑week program. It focuses on adequate energy, protein, fluids, micronutrients, and simple habits that fit postpartum life. Always defer to the OB/primary care provider, registered dietitian, and any specific medical advice (e.g., thyroid issues, diabetes, food allergies). If milk supply, weight change, or energy feel off, adjust and/or refer to an RD.

Guiding principles
- Energy: Most breastfeeding parents need about +300–500 kcal/day above baseline. Start modestly (+350 kcal/day) and adjust to hunger, weight trend (aim ≤0.5 kg/1 lb per week loss if weight loss is desired), mood, and milk supply.
- Protein: Target 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight per day. Distribute evenly across 3 meals + 1–2 snacks (20–35 g protein per meal).
- Carbohydrates: 45–60% of calories from slow‑digesting, fiber‑rich sources to support milk production and energy.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories with emphasis on mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats; include omega‑3s (DHA/EPA).
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day to support bowel regularity. Increase gradually and pair with fluids.
- Fluids: Start with ~3+ liters/day total fluid. Use thirst, urine color (pale straw), and feeding frequency to guide. Add 250–500 mL around nursing/pumping sessions.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal vitamin per provider. Emphasize calcium, iron, iodine, choline, vitamin D, and omega‑3s.

Daily plate template
- Each main meal:
  - Palm to hand‑size protein (20–35 g): eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, poultry, fish (see safety), lean red meat, tofu/tempeh, legumes plus grains, protein oats or smoothie.
  - 1–2 fists vegetables (mix cooked/raw), especially leafy greens, crucifers, orange/red veg.
  - 1–2 cupped‑hand servings carbs: oats, quinoa, whole‑grain bread/wraps, brown rice, potatoes/sweet potatoes, fruit.
  - 1–2 thumbs fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts/nut butter, seeds (chia/flax/hemp), tahini.
- Snacks (choose 1–2/day): 10–20 g protein + fiber + fluid. Examples below.

Key nutrients for lactation
- Protein: tissue repair, milk components. Aim 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day.
- DHA/EPA: infant neurodevelopment. Eat low‑mercury fatty fish 2–3x/week (e.g., salmon, sardines, trout) or take algae/fish oil providing 300–600 mg DHA daily after provider approval.
- Choline: 450–550 mg/day. Eggs (especially yolks), lean meats, soy, beans. Consider choline‑containing prenatal if low intake.
- Iodine: 290 mcg/day. Use iodized salt; dairy, eggs, seafood. If dairy‑free, consider supplement per provider.
- Vitamin D: Many need 1500–2000 IU/day; confirm with provider/testing. Supplement is often recommended.
- Iron: Maintain stores, especially if postpartum anemia. Red meat, legumes, fortified cereals; pair plant iron with vitamin C sources. Avoid excess supplemental iron unless prescribed.
- Calcium: 1000 mg/day (1300 mg if under 19). Dairy or fortified alt milks, yogurt, cheese, tofu set with calcium sulfate, leafy greens, almonds.
- B12: Ensure adequate if vegetarian/vegan—supplement as needed.

Simple 1‑week rotating meal plan (repeat and mix‑and‑match)
- Breakfast options
  - Protein oats: 1/2–3/4 cup oats cooked in milk/alt milk + 1 scoop whey/plant protein + chia/flax + berries + peanut butter.
  - 2 eggs + 2 egg whites scramble with spinach/mushrooms + whole‑grain toast + fruit.
  - Greek yogurt bowl (1.5–2 cups) with granola, mixed berries, hemp seeds, honey.
  - Smoothie: milk/alt milk + Greek yogurt or protein powder + banana + frozen berries + spinach + chia + 1 tbsp peanut/almond butter.
- Lunch options
  - Whole‑grain wrap: chicken or tofu, hummus, mixed greens, cucumber, tomato, avocado. Side fruit.
  - Quinoa bowl: quinoa, roasted sweet potato, black beans, salsa, cabbage slaw, olive oil/lime, feta or avocado.
  - Salmon salad (canned) with olive‑oil vinaigrette on mixed greens + whole‑grain crackers.
- Dinner options
  - Baked salmon or trout, roasted potatoes, broccoli, side salad.
  - Turkey or lentil chili over brown rice; add Greek yogurt and avocado.
  - Stir‑fry: tofu/shrimp/chicken with mixed veg, edamame, served over jasmine or brown rice; sesame oil finish.
  - Pasta night: whole‑grain or chickpea pasta, tomato sauce, extra‑lean ground beef/turkey or white beans, side salad, parmesan.
- Snacks
  - Cottage cheese + pineapple; or Greek yogurt + fruit.
  - Apple/banana + peanut/almond butter.
  - Hummus + whole‑grain pita + carrots/cukes.
  - Trail mix (nuts/seeds + a few dark chocolate chips).
  - Cheese stick + whole‑grain crackers.
  - Protein shake with milk/alt milk + fruit.
  - Chia pudding made with milk/alt milk.

Timing and feeding
- Eat to hunger; avoid long stretches without fuel. Many do well with 3 meals + 1–2 snacks.
- Pre‑feed snack (if a session is near): yogurt and fruit, toast with nut butter, or a small smoothie.
- Post‑exercise: within 60 minutes, aim for 20–30 g protein + carbs (e.g., turkey sandwich + fruit; yogurt + granola; smoothie).
- Night feeds: Keep a bedside water bottle and an easy snack if needed (e.g., trail mix, protein bar).

Safe fish and food safety notes
- Choose low‑mercury fish: salmon, sardines, trout, pollock, tilapia, shrimp, canned light tuna (limit albacore to 1 serving/week). Aim 2–3 servings/week total.
- Avoid high‑mercury fish: shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish (Gulf), bigeye tuna.
- Food safety: Wash produce, fully cook meats/eggs/seafood, reheat leftovers thoroughly. Limit alcohol per provider guidance; if drinking, time feeds/pumping with a conservative window.

Hydration strategies
- Start day with 500 mL water.
- Drink a glass at each feed/pump.
- Flavor water with lemon, cucumber, or use herbal teas/broths.
- Include electrolytes during longer walks or hot days (low‑sugar options).

Supplements (confirm with provider)
- Prenatal/postnatal multivitamin with iodine and choline.
- Vitamin D3 (commonly 1500–2000 IU/day) based on labs/advice.
- DHA (300–600 mg/day).
- Iron only if deficient/anemic.
- Consider magnesium glycinate (100–200 mg at night) for sleep/muscle relaxation if approved.

Special considerations
- Milk supply: Primary drivers are frequent effective milk removal, hydration, and adequate energy. If supply dips, increase fluids and calories slightly (+150–250 kcal), add an extra snack, and work with a lactation consultant.
- GI comfort: Increase fiber gradually; use warm fluids, prunes/kiwi/chia pudding to support bowel movements. Exhale on exertion in the bathroom; avoid straining.
- Weight changes: Early months prioritize recovery, milk supply, and strength. If pursuing fat loss later, keep deficit small (~250 kcal/day) and monitor supply/energy.

Grocery list starter
- Proteins: eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr/cottage cheese, chicken/turkey, salmon/sardines/tuna (light), tofu/tempeh, beans/lentils, edamame, protein powder.
- Carbs: oats, whole‑grain bread/wraps, rice, quinoa, potatoes/sweet potatoes, pasta (incl. chickpea/lentil), fruit (berries, bananas, apples, citrus), tortillas.
- Veg: spinach, kale, broccoli, peppers, carrots, onions, tomatoes, cucumbers, mixed salad greens, frozen veg.
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, nut butters, seeds (chia/flax/hemp), olives, tahini.
- Dairy/alt dairy: milk or fortified almond/soy/oat milk.
- Extras: iodized salt, spices, salsa, broth, dark chocolate, herbal teas.

How to use with training weeks
- Weeks 4–6: Focus on consistency—3 meals + 1–2 snacks, hydration habit at each feed, simple protein‑forward breakfasts, easy batch dinners.
- Weeks 7–10: Add a post‑walk/post‑session protein + carb snack. Introduce 2–3 fish meals/week if not already.
- Weeks 11–12: Fine‑tune portions to energy needs (increase if fatigue/hunger/supply dips; reduce slightly if aiming for gentle fat loss and supply is robust).

Red flags/when to refer
- Rapid weight loss, persistent fatigue, dizziness, signs of nutrient deficiency (hair loss beyond normal postpartum shedding, brittle nails, mouth sores), constipation unresponsive to diet, or milk supply concerns—refer to OB/PCP and a registered dietitian; consult lactation support as needed.

Great—here’s a clear add-on that layers progressive, safe strength work into the early postpartum weeks while respecting the initial restrictions. It plugs directly into the original plan and flags exactly when and how to add load, tempo, and unilateral control from Weeks 4–8, then bridges into the already-defined Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12).

Guiding principles for early strength
- Stay symptom-led: progress only if no pain at incision, no increased bleeding, no pelvic heaviness/pressure or urinary leakage, and no midline doming.
- Exhale on exertion; no breath-holding. Use 20–30% core/pelvic floor effort to “zip up” on the exhale.
- Use household objects for load (water jugs, backpack with books, cans), keeping RPE 3–5/10 in Weeks 4–6 and 4–6/10 in Weeks 7–8.
- Add only one variable at a time: range, reps, tempo, then load.

Weeks 4–5 (still light activity only; no heavy lifting, no impact, no direct abs)
Frequency: 3 movement sessions/week (+ walking)

Add gentle strength emphasis within Sessions A/B:
- Squat pattern
  - Week 4: Sit-to-stand 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps, slow 2–3s down, exhale to stand. Add a light counterbalance (hands forward).
  - Week 5: Progress to air squat to high target or keep sit-to-stand and add tempo 3s down/1s pause/stand. Option: hold a 2–4 kg household load close to chest if 100% symptom-free.
- Hip bridge
  - Week 4: Bridge 2 x 6–8 with 2–3s hold at top.
  - Week 5: 2–3 x 8–10; add isometric abduction by gently pressing knees out into hands or a mini band (if available) for 8–10 reps.
- Hip hinge patterning (no load yet)
  - Week 5: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps with broomstick/dowel along back (head–thoracic–sacrum contact). Focus on ribs-over-pelvis, slight knee bend, hinge from hips.
- Upper body push (incline)
  - Week 4: Wall push-up 2 x 6–8, exhale on push, ribs stacked.
  - Week 5: 2–3 x 8–10 at wall or progress to higher countertop if easy.
- Upper body pull/scapular control
  - Week 4: Wall scapular slides 2 x 8–10.
  - Week 5: Add isometric rows: loop a towel around a post, create tension and hold 10–15s x 3–4 holds, 1–2 rounds; or keep slides and add prone T/Y raises on pillows (short range) 2 x 8–10.
- Lateral hip/glute
  - Week 4: Side-lying clamshells 2 x 8/side (bodyweight).
  - Week 5: 2–3 x 10–12/side. Add light band at Week 6 if cleared to progress.
- Calves
  - Week 4: Double-leg calf raises 2 x 10–12 at counter.
  - Week 5: 2–3 x 12–15, slow 2s up/2s down.

Notes
- Keep core-specific drills “deep core friendly” only (heel slides, breathing, pelvic clocks). Stop any drill that causes doming/pressure.

Week 6 (after OB clearance to progress; begin foundational loading)
Frequency: 3–4 sessions/week; use A/B split below. Keep RPE 4–5/10.

Session A (Lower-Body Strength Emphasis)
- Squat to box or air squat: 3 sets x 8–12. Option to hold 2–6 kg front-loaded object by Week 6. Tempo 2–3s down.
- Hip hinge with backpack (front-hold or hugged): 3 x 8–10. Start very light (2–4 kg) to mid-shin range.
- Step-ups to 4–6" step: 3 x 8/side; use support; slow down, controlled up.
- Bridge progressions: 3 x 10–12, add 3–5s hold at top; optional light load across hips (folded towel under object for comfort).
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–15; add 1–2s pause at top.

Session B (Upper + Core-Friendly Strength)
- Incline push-up (countertop): 3 x 8–12; lower the incline as able.
- Tall-kneeling or half-kneeling isometric press (hands pressing into wall at chest height): 3 x 15–20s holds; ribs stacked.
- Bird-dog (opposite arm/leg) or arms-only if needed: 3 x 6–8/side with 2s pause.
- Isometric towel row (seated or standing): 3 x 10–15s holds x 2–3 reps; or bent-over backpack row 2–3 x 8–10 light load if posture stable.
- Side-lying clamshells: 3 x 12–15/side; add mini band if no symptoms.

Optional “Capacity Finisher” (only if feeling good)
- 6-minute EMOM alternating:
  - Minute 1: Sit-to-stand x 10–12
  - Minute 2: Incline push-ups x 8–10
Keep breathing steady (RPE ≤5).

Week 7 progression (still no impact; avoid long forearm planks/sit-ups if doming)
- Increase one variable per exercise:
  - Load: +1–2 kg to squats/hinges if RPE ≤5 and zero symptoms.
  - Tempo: Squat 3–1–1 (3s down, 1s pause, 1s up). Hinge 2–1–2.
  - Range: Step-ups to 6–8" if knee/hip happy.
- Add unilateral stability:
  - Split-stance squat to box (supported): 3 x 6–8/side.
  - Marching bridge: 3 x 8/side keeping pelvis level.
  - Single-arm backpack row (elbow to hip): 3 x 8–10/side, light.
- Upper push:
  - Lower the incline slightly or add 1–2 reps per set.
- Core control:
  - Dead bug heel taps or single-leg extensions 2–3 x 6–8/side if no doming. Otherwise keep with heel slides and bird-dog.

Week 8 progression (bridge to Phase 3)
- Lower-body loading:
  - Goblet squat (backpack/weight) 3 x 8–10 at RPE 5–6.
  - Hip hinge (Romanian deadlift pattern) 3 x 8–10; add slow 3s eccentric.
  - Step-ups 3 x 8–10/side with light load held at chest if rock-solid.
  - Supported split-squat 3 x 6–8/side, short range; add load only if perfect.
- Upper body:
  - Incline push-ups 3 x 10–12; move to sturdy table height if countertop is easy.
  - Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side; add brief 1s squeeze at top.
  - Wall slide to Y 3 x 10–12; add mini lift-off if shoulder control allows.
- Core-friendly anti-movement
  - Tall-kneeling anti-rotation (Pallof) with band if available 3 x 10–12/side, or long-lever isometric wall press 3 x 15–20s.
- Capacity option (RPE ≤6)
  - Circuit x 2–3 rounds:
    - Sit-to-stand or goblet squat x 10–12
    - Hinge x 10
    - Step-ups x 8/side
    - Incline push-ups x 10
    Rest 60–75s as needed.

How to coach progression and safety checks
- Weekly readiness check: sleep, soreness, incision comfort, bleeding, pelvic floor symptoms, and doming. If any red flags, pull back to the last asymptomatic variation.
- Breathing cue: inhale to prepare, exhale through the effort. If you catch a breath-hold, reduce load or range.
- Pressure management: if coning appears on squats or hinges, lighten load, shorten range, or modify stance; revisit 360 breathing and “zip” on exhale.
- Volume caps early: keep total working sets per pattern at 6–9 sets per week (e.g., squats + step-ups combined) in Weeks 6–8.

Equipment notes for home
- Loads: backpack with books, water jugs, laundry detergent, tote with cans.
- Steps: low, stable step or bottom stair.
- Support: chair/countertop/doorframe for balance on split-stance and step-ups.
- Bands: optional mini band for clamshells and a long loop for press-outs/rows if available.

Transition into Weeks 9–12
- If Week 8 is symptom-free at RPE 5–6, follow the Phase 3 plan as written, using the heaviest household loads that still allow good breathing and control.
- Add tempo or an extra set before adding more load.

- Main Set
  - Heel slides 2 x 8/side.

- Mobility: cat-cow 8–10; open books 6–8/side; lateral hip shifts at wall 6/side.
- Main Set
  - Sit-to-stand 3 x 8.
  - Bridge 2–3 x 8–10 with 3–5s hold.
  - Clamshells 2 x 10/side.
  - Standing overhead reach to calf raise 2 x 8–10.

Session B (25–30 min)
- Breath/PF as above.
- Main Set
  - Heel slides 2 x 8/side.
  - Marching bridge 2 x 6–8/side.
  - Wall push-ups 2 x 8.
  - Wall scap slides or isometric towel row 2 x 10–15s x 3 holds.

- 15–30 min easy walk; 8–10 min stretch + downregulation breathing.

2) Main (2–3 rounds; RPE 5)

- Hip hinge (RDL pattern) with very light load 8–10 to mid-shin.
- Step-ups to 4–6" step 8/side, supported.
- Bridge with 3–5s hold 10–12.
3) Accessory: Calf raises 2 x 12–15; Clamshells 2 x 12–15/side.
4) Cool-down: breathing + gentle hip flexor stretch.

2) Main (2–3 rounds; RPE 5)

- Single-arm row (light backpack/water jug) 8–10/side.
- Bird-dog (opposite arm/leg) 6–8/side with 2–3s pause.
- Wall slides to Y 10–12.
3) Accessory: Marching bridge 8–10/side; Anti-rotation wall press or Pallof (band) 2 x 15–20s/side.
4) Cool-down.

- Circuit x 2–3 rounds: Sit-to-stand or light goblet squat x 10–12; Hinge x 10; Step-back lunge tap or split-stance sit-to-stand x 6–8/side; Incline push-up x 8–10. Rest 60–75s.

- 360 breathing reset 1–2 sets.
- Heel slides 2 x 6–8/side.
- Marching bridge 2 x 6–8/side.
- Bird-dog 2 x 6–8/side.
- Optional short-lever side plank (knees) 2 x 10–20s/side if zero symptoms.

- RDL 3 x 8–10 light load.

- Bridge 3 x 10–12 with 3–5s hold.
- Calf raises 3 x 12–15.

- Incline push-up 3 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side, 1s squeeze at top.

- Bridge march or bridge with gentle abduction 3 x 8–10.

- Dead bug A (heel taps or single-leg extension) 2–3 x 6–8/side.
- Side plank (knees) 2 x 15–25s/side if symptom-free.
- Anti-rotation press (band) 3 x 8–10/side with 2s hold.
- Mobility flow: thoracic, hip flexor, calves, chest.

Conditioning Day (low impact)
- Brisk walk intervals 25–35 minutes or circuit 2–3 rounds at RPE 5–6:
  - Goblet squat x 10–12
  - Step-back lunge tap x 8/side
  - Incline push-up x 10–12
  - Hinge x 10

WEEK 6 (Postpartum Week 8): Capacity and control (no jumping)
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Goblet squat 3 x 8–12; option +1–2 kg if RPE ≤6 and breathing solid.
- RDL 3 x 8–12 with 2–3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 8–10/side; add light load at chest if stable.
- Supported split-squat 3 x 6–8/side (short–moderate range).
- Calf raises 3 x 12–15.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up (lower surface if ready) 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Tall/half-kneeling wall press isometric or band press-out 3 x 15–20s or 10–12.
- Side plank (knees) 2–3 x 15–25s/side.
- Dead bug A/B depending on tolerance 2–3 x 6–8/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing 2 sets.
- Quadruped hover (short lever bear) 10–15s x 2–3 if zero symptoms; else bird-dog.
- Anti-extension forearm-to-wall plank 2 x 15–20s.
- Mobility flow 8–10 min.

Conditioning Day
- Walk 30–45 minutes with 4–5 x 2–3 minute brisk intervals; modest hills okay.

Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat 3–4 x 8–12; add load or a 4th set if RPE ≤6.
- RDL 3 x 8–12, 2–3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 10/side, slow down phase.
- Split-squat 3 x 8/side, supported.
- Finisher: Calf raises 2 x 15–20.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up: 3–4 x 8–12; lower surface if strong.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side, 1s pause.
- Anti-rotation press or wall press 3 x 10–12 or 20–30s.
- Dead bug B (arm + opposite leg reach, small range) 2–3 x 5–6/side.
- Side plank (knees) 2–3 x 20–25s/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing reset + thoracic/hip mobility 10–12 min.
- Quadruped hover holds 10–15s x 2–3; or bird-dog if any symptoms.

Conditioning Day
- Walk 35–45 minutes with 5–6 x 3-minute brisk intervals or 3–4 rounds low-impact circuit (goblet squat, step-ups, incline push-up, hinge) at RPE 5–6.

- RDL 3 x 8–10; 3s down, 1s pause below knees.
- Step-ups 3 x 10/side with brief mid-range pause.
- Supported split-squat 3 x 8–10/side (slow eccentric).

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up toward lower surface 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Bird-dog 3 x 8/side with 2–3s pause.
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension press or forearm-to-wall plank 2–3 x 15–25s.
- Side plank (knees) or short-lever forearm plank 2–3 x 15–25s (only if zero doming).

Core/Mobility Day
- Dead bug C (full arm + leg extension) 2–3 x 5/side only if flawless; otherwise hold Week 7–9 level.
- Glute bridge single-leg ISO (partial range) 2 x 8–10/side.
- Mobility flow 10–12 min.

Conditioning Day (low impact; still no jumping)
- Brisk walk 40–50 minutes or EMOM 10–12 min alternating:
  - Minute 1: Step-ups x 10–12
  - Minute 2: Incline push-ups x 8–12
  Keep breath steady.

Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Goblet squat 4 x 8–10 (progress load/tempo as tolerated).
- RDL 3 x 8–10 with 3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 10–12/side.
- Split-squat 3 x 8–10/side.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Push-up incline as low as good form allows 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Anti-rotation press 3 x 10–12/side with 2s hold.
- Side plank (knees or staggered) 2–3 x 20–25s.
- Dead bug C or B based on symptoms 2–3 x 5–6/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- Bear hover holds 10–15s x 2–3; or regress to bird-dog if symptoms.
- Tall-kneeling chops/lifts (band) 2–3 x 8–10/side.
- Mobility 10 min.

Conditioning Day
- Option A (introduce tiny impact if fully symptom-free): Impact primer 1–2x/week
  - 3–4 rounds: Marching in place 60s; Fast step-ups 30s; Heel-to-toe quick walk 30s; Rest 60–90s.
  - Optional very low-amplitude ankle bounces (heels kiss floor) 2 x 20–30s only if zero symptoms.
- Option B (remain low-impact): Brisk walk 40–50 min with hills or 3–4 rounds low-impact circuit at RPE 5–6.

WEEK 10 (Postpartum Week 12): Option to build tiny impact doses or continue low-impact
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat 4 x 8–12, moderate load/tempo.
- RDL 3 x 8–10, 3s down.
- Step-ups 3 x 10–12/side.
- Split-squat 3 x 8–10/side.
- Low-impact “power” intent: fast but quiet sit-to-stand to tall reach 2 x 8 (no jump).

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline or floor push-up test sets 3–4 x 6–10 (only if zero doming).
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension press or elevated plank 2–3 x 15–25s.
- Side plank (knees or full if ready) 2–3 x 15–25s.

Core/Mobility Day
- Maintain best-tolerated dead bug/bear/anti-rotation variations 10–12 minutes.
- Mobility flow 10–12 minutes.

Conditioning Day
- If impact tolerated last week: include 2–3 x 15–20s very gentle hops in place or phantom jump-rope between brisk walking bouts; rest 60–90s; stop at first symptom.
- If not, continue low-impact intervals/circuit at RPE 5–6.

BREASTFEEDING-SUPPORTIVE NUTRITION AND RECOVERY (apply across all weeks)
- Energy: Start about +350 kcal/day over baseline while breastfeeding; adjust to hunger, energy, supply, and weight trend (aim loss ≤0.5 kg/1 lb per week if pursuing).
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day, distributed across meals/snacks (20–35 g per meal).
- Carbs/fats: Emphasize fiber-rich carbs (45–60% kcal) and healthy fats (25–35% kcal); include omega-3s (DHA/EPA 300–600 mg/day from low-mercury fish 2–3x/week or algae/fish oil if approved).
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal per provider; prioritize iodine (iodized salt, dairy/eggs/seafood), choline (eggs, soy, meats/beans), vitamin D (often 1500–2000 IU/day; confirm), iron (as needed), calcium (1000 mg/day).
- Fluids: Target ~3+ L/day; sip at each feed/pump; pale straw urine as guide. Add 250–500 mL around workouts/hot days.
- Meal structure: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Post-exercise: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 60 minutes.
- Snack ideas: Greek yogurt + berries; cottage cheese + fruit; apple + nut butter; hummus + veg + pita; protein smoothie; chia pudding.
- GI care: Increase fiber gradually; warm fluids, prunes/kiwi/chia; avoid straining—exhale on bowel movements.
- Sleep/recovery: Flexible training volume on low-sleep days; keep at least one mobility/breath-only session weekly. Consider brief high-waist supportive garments for comfort (not tight binders).

PROGRESSION AND COACHING NOTES
- Add only one variable at a time: reps, tempo, range, or load.
- Watch the midline for doming and monitor pelvic floor symptoms at all new steps.
- Keep core blocks short and high-quality (8–12 minutes), 2–3x/week.
- If any setbacks or symptoms, return to the last asymptomatic variation and consider referral to a pelvic health physical therapist.

This consolidated plan keeps her steadily progressing from restorative movement to moderate strength and optional light impact by Weeks 11–12, while aligning with OB guidance and postpartum best practices.

Here’s the consolidated 12-week postpartum return plan from Week 1 (four weeks postpartum) through Week 12, with all adjustments rolled in: OB clearance milestones, no jumping through Week 10, progressive strength, safe core reintroduction, walking/conditioning, and breastfeeding-supportive nutrition and recovery. Home-based with a yoga mat and optional household loads/bands.

Global guardrails
- Stop and regress if: increased bleeding, incision pain/redness, pelvic heaviness/pressure or bulge, urinary/fecal leakage, fever, calf pain/swelling, dizziness, sharp abdominal pain, or visible midline doming/coning.
- Breathing and pressure: inhale to prepare, exhale on effort; avoid breath-holding/straining. Gentle pelvic floor and deep-core engagement (20–30% effort) on exhale; fully release on inhale.
- Intensity by phase: Weeks 1–2 RPE 3–4; Weeks 3–6 RPE 3–4 (light) until medical clearance; Weeks 7–10 RPE 5–6 (moderate, no jumping); Weeks 11–12 RPE 5–6 with optional tiny doses of impact only if symptom-free.
- Equipment: yoga mat; chair/counter; optional backpack/water jugs; low step (4–8"); optional mini/long band.

WEEK 1 (Postpartum Week 4): Restore and reconnect
Frequency: 3 movement sessions + easy walks most days (flat, conversational)

Walking
- 10–20 minutes/day, break into 5–10 minute chunks if needed.

Session A (20–25 min)
1) Breath/Pelvic Floor (5–6 min)
- 360 breathing in side-lying or hook-lying: 2 sets x 6–8 breaths.
- Gentle pelvic floor lift on exhale (blueberry lift), full release on inhale: 6–8 reps.

2) Mobility/Activation (6–8 min)
- Neck/shoulder rolls x 5 each way.
- Cat-cow (small range) x 6–8.
- Pelvic clocks (tiny) x 5–8 each direction.
- Seated/standing thoracic rotations x 6/side.
- Ankle pumps/circles x 10/side.

3) Main Set (8–10 min)
- Sit-to-stand (high chair) 2–3 x 6–8, slow 2–3s down, exhale to stand.
- Mini glute bridge 2 x 6–8 with 2–3s hold.
- Heel slides (supine) 2 x 6–8/side (stop if doming).
- Wall scapular slides 2 x 8–10.

Cool-down: 2 minutes easy breathing.

Optional Light Day (10–15 min)
- Supported child’s pose, doorway chest stretch, calf stretch, 20–30s x 2 each; 5-minute breathing.

WEEK 2 (Postpartum Week 5): Light capacity build
Walking
- 15–25 minutes/day, add a few minutes every other day as tolerated.

Session A (22–28 min)
- 360 breathing reset: 2 x 6–8 breaths.
- Mobility: as Week 1, add open books x 6/side.
- Main Set (10–14 min)
  - Sit-to-stand 2–3 x 8–10.
  - Bridge 2–3 x 8–10; add gentle abduction (press knees into hands/towel).
  - Side-lying clamshells (bodyweight) 2 x 8–10/side.
  - Wall scap slides 2 x 8–10.

Session B (22–28 min)
- Breath + mobility as above.
- Main Set
  - Heel slides 2 x 8/side.
  - Marching bridge (heel lifts) 2 x 6/side.
  - Calf raises (double-leg, at counter) 2 x 10–12.
  - Wall push-up (gentle) 2 x 6–8.

Notes
- Keep intensity light; no impact, no heavy lifting, no direct “abs” beyond deep-core friendly drills. Watch for doming.

WEEK 3 (Postpartum Week 6, pre-appointment): Maintain light progression
Walking
- 20–30 minutes/day comfortable; keep flat terrain.

Session A (25–30 min)
- Breath/PF: 2 x 6–8 breaths; 6–8 gentle lifts.
- Mobility: cat-cow 8–10; open books 6–8/side; lateral hip shifts at wall 6/side.
- Main Set
  - Sit-to-stand 3 x 8.
  - Bridge 2–3 x 8–10 with 3–5s hold.
  - Clamshells 2 x 10/side.
  - Standing overhead reach to calf raise 2 x 8–10.

Session B (25–30 min)
- Breath/PF as above.
- Main Set
  - Heel slides 2 x 8/side.
  - Marching bridge 2 x 6–8/side.
  - Wall push-ups 2 x 8.
  - Wall scap slides or isometric towel row 2 x 10–15s x 3 holds.

Recovery/Mobility Day
- 15–30 min easy walk; 8–10 min stretch + downregulation breathing.

WEEK 4 (Postpartum Week 6+, after clearance visit)
- Clearance outcome: Cleared for moderate exercise; no jumping for four more weeks (through end of Week 10). Begin moderate progression now.

Walking/Conditioning
- 25–35 minutes most days; optionally 2 x 2-minute brisk intervals with 3-minute easy between if asymptomatic.

Session A: Lower Emphasis (30–35 min)
1) Prep (5–6 min): 360 breathing 2 x 6; hip/ankle mobility.
2) Main (2–3 rounds; RPE 5)
- Squat to box or light goblet squat (2–4 kg) 8–12, 2–3s down.
- Hip hinge (RDL pattern) with very light load 8–10 to mid-shin.
- Step-ups to 4–6" step 8/side, supported.
- Bridge with 3–5s hold 10–12.
3) Accessory: Calf raises 2 x 12–15; Clamshells 2 x 12–15/side.
4) Cool-down: breathing + gentle hip flexor stretch.

Session B: Upper/Core-Friendly (30–35 min)
1) Prep: breathing + thoracic openers (5–6 min).
2) Main (2–3 rounds; RPE 5)
- Incline push-up (counter) 8–12.
- Single-arm row (light backpack/water jug) 8–10/side.
- Bird-dog (opposite arm/leg) 6–8/side with 2–3s pause.
- Wall slides to Y 10–12.
3) Accessory: Marching bridge 8–10/side; Anti-rotation wall press or Pallof (band) 2 x 15–20s/side.
4) Cool-down.

Optional Session C: Full-Body Capacity (25–30 min; RPE ≤5)
- Circuit x 2–3 rounds: Sit-to-stand or light goblet squat x 10–12; Hinge x 10; Step-back lunge tap or split-stance sit-to-stand x 6–8/side; Incline push-up x 8–10. Rest 60–75s.

Core Block focus this week (insert 10–12 min into 2–3 sessions)
- 360 breathing reset 1–2 sets.
- Heel slides 2 x 6–8/side.
- Marching bridge 2 x 6–8/side.
- Bird-dog 2 x 6–8/side.
- Optional short-lever side plank (knees) 2 x 10–20s/side if zero symptoms.

WEEK 5 (Postpartum Week 7): Moderate build (no jumping)
Walking/Conditioning
- 30–40 minutes with 3–4 x 2-minute brisk intervals, easy between.

Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Goblet squat 3 x 8–10 (RPE 5–6), 2–3s eccentric.
- RDL 3 x 8–10 light load.
- Step-ups 3 x 8–10/side, supported.
- Bridge 3 x 10–12 with 3–5s hold.
- Calf raises 3 x 12–15.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Posterior Chain)
- Incline push-up 3 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side, 1s squeeze at top.
- Bird-dog slow tempo 3 x 6–8/side.
- Wall slides or prone T/Y on pillows 3 x 10–12.
- Bridge march or bridge with gentle abduction 3 x 8–10.

Core/Mobility Day (10–15 min core + 8–10 min mobility)
- Dead bug A (heel taps or single-leg extension) 2–3 x 6–8/side.
- Side plank (knees) 2 x 15–25s/side if symptom-free.
- Anti-rotation press (band) 3 x 8–10/side with 2s hold.
- Mobility flow: thoracic, hip flexor, calves, chest.

Conditioning Day (low impact)
- Brisk walk intervals 25–35 minutes or circuit 2–3 rounds at RPE 5–6:
  - Goblet squat x 10–12
  - Step-back lunge tap x 8/side
  - Incline push-up x 10–12
  - Hinge x 10

WEEK 6 (Postpartum Week 8): Capacity and control (no jumping)
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Goblet squat 3 x 8–12; option +1–2 kg if RPE ≤6 and breathing solid.
- RDL 3 x 8–12 with 2–3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 8–10/side; add light load at chest if stable.
- Supported split-squat 3 x 6–8/side (short–moderate range).
- Calf raises 3 x 12–15.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up (lower surface if ready) 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Tall/half-kneeling wall press isometric or band press-out 3 x 15–20s or 10–12.
- Side plank (knees) 2–3 x 15–25s/side.
- Dead bug A/B depending on tolerance 2–3 x 6–8/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing 2 sets.
- Quadruped hover (short lever bear) 10–15s x 2–3 if zero symptoms; else bird-dog.
- Anti-extension forearm-to-wall plank 2 x 15–20s.
- Mobility flow 8–10 min.

Conditioning Day
- Walk 30–45 minutes with 4–5 x 2–3 minute brisk intervals; modest hills okay.

WEEK 7 (Postpartum Week 9): Strength endurance (no jumping)
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat 3–4 x 8–12; add load or a 4th set if RPE ≤6.
- RDL 3 x 8–12, 2–3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 10/side, slow down phase.
- Split-squat 3 x 8/side, supported.
- Finisher: Calf raises 2 x 15–20.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up: 3–4 x 8–12; lower surface if strong.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side, 1s pause.
- Anti-rotation press or wall press 3 x 10–12 or 20–30s.
- Dead bug B (arm + opposite leg reach, small range) 2–3 x 5–6/side.
- Side plank (knees) 2–3 x 20–25s/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- 360 breathing reset + thoracic/hip mobility 10–12 min.
- Quadruped hover holds 10–15s x 2–3; or bird-dog if any symptoms.

Conditioning Day
- Walk 35–45 minutes with 5–6 x 3-minute brisk intervals or 3–4 rounds low-impact circuit (goblet squat, step-ups, incline push-up, hinge) at RPE 5–6.

WEEK 8 (Postpartum Week 10): Consolidate; prep for later impact
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat 4 x 8–10; 3s down/1s pause if technique allows.
- RDL 3 x 8–10; 3s down, 1s pause below knees.
- Step-ups 3 x 10/side with brief mid-range pause.
- Supported split-squat 3 x 8–10/side (slow eccentric).

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline push-up toward lower surface 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Bird-dog 3 x 8/side with 2–3s pause.
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension press or forearm-to-wall plank 2–3 x 15–25s.
- Side plank (knees) or short-lever forearm plank 2–3 x 15–25s (only if zero doming).

Core/Mobility Day
- Dead bug C (full arm + leg extension) 2–3 x 5/side only if flawless; otherwise hold Week 7–9 level.
- Glute bridge single-leg ISO (partial range) 2 x 8–10/side.
- Mobility flow 10–12 min.

Conditioning Day (low impact; still no jumping)
- Brisk walk 40–50 minutes or EMOM 10–12 min alternating:
  - Minute 1: Step-ups x 10–12
  - Minute 2: Incline push-ups x 8–12
  Keep breath steady.

WEEK 9 (Postpartum Week 11): Impact may start if symptom-free (tiny doses)
Readiness checks before adding impact
- Can perform: 10–12 single-leg step-downs/side (6–8" step) with control; 30s marching in place; 20 calf raises; side plank (knees) 20s/side; no coning with squats/hinges/push-ups. If not met, remain low-impact.

Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Goblet squat 4 x 8–10 (progress load/tempo as tolerated).
- RDL 3 x 8–10 with 3s eccentric.
- Step-ups 3 x 10–12/side.
- Split-squat 3 x 8–10/side.

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Push-up incline as low as good form allows 3–4 x 8–12.
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Anti-rotation press 3 x 10–12/side with 2s hold.
- Side plank (knees or staggered) 2–3 x 20–25s.
- Dead bug C or B based on symptoms 2–3 x 5–6/side.

Core/Mobility Day
- Bear hover holds 10–15s x 2–3; or regress to bird-dog if symptoms.
- Tall-kneeling chops/lifts (band) 2–3 x 8–10/side.
- Mobility 10 min.

Conditioning Day
- Option A (introduce tiny impact if fully symptom-free): Impact primer 1–2x/week
  - 3–4 rounds: Marching in place 60s; Fast step-ups 30s; Heel-to-toe quick walk 30s; Rest 60–90s.
  - Optional very low-amplitude ankle bounces (heels kiss floor) 2 x 20–30s only if zero symptoms.
- Option B (remain low-impact): Brisk walk 40–50 min with hills or 3–4 rounds low-impact circuit at RPE 5–6.

WEEK 10 (Postpartum Week 12): Option to build tiny impact doses or continue low-impact
Strength Day 1 (Lower)
- Squat 4 x 8–12, moderate load/tempo.
- RDL 3 x 8–10, 3s down.
- Step-ups 3 x 10–12/side.
- Split-squat 3 x 8–10/side.
- Low-impact “power” intent: fast but quiet sit-to-stand to tall reach 2 x 8 (no jump).

Strength Day 2 (Upper + Core)
- Incline or floor push-up test sets 3–4 x 6–10 (only if zero doming).
- Single-arm row 3 x 10–12/side.
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension press or elevated plank 2–3 x 15–25s.
- Side plank (knees or full if ready) 2–3 x 15–25s.

Core/Mobility Day
- Maintain best-tolerated dead bug/bear/anti-rotation variations 10–12 minutes.
- Mobility flow 10–12 minutes.

Conditioning Day
- If impact tolerated last week: include 2–3 x 15–20s very gentle hops in place or phantom jump-rope between brisk walking bouts; rest 60–90s; stop at first symptom.
- If not, continue low-impact intervals/circuit at RPE 5–6.

BREASTFEEDING-SUPPORTIVE NUTRITION AND RECOVERY (apply across all weeks)
- Energy: Start about +350 kcal/day over baseline while breastfeeding; adjust to hunger, energy, supply, and weight trend (aim loss ≤0.5 kg/1 lb per week if pursuing).
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day, distributed across meals/snacks (20–35 g per meal).
- Carbs/fats: Emphasize fiber-rich carbs (45–60% kcal) and healthy fats (25–35% kcal); include omega-3s (DHA/EPA 300–600 mg/day from low-mercury fish 2–3x/week or algae/fish oil if approved).
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal/postnatal per provider; prioritize iodine (iodized salt, dairy/eggs/seafood), choline (eggs, soy, meats/beans), vitamin D (often 1500–2000 IU/day; confirm), iron (as needed), calcium (1000 mg/day).
- Fluids: Target ~3+ L/day; sip at each feed/pump; pale straw urine as guide. Add 250–500 mL around workouts/hot days.
- Meal structure: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Post-exercise: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 60 minutes.
- Snack ideas: Greek yogurt + berries; cottage cheese + fruit; apple + nut butter; hummus + veg + pita; protein smoothie; chia pudding.
- GI care: Increase fiber gradually; warm fluids, prunes/kiwi/chia; avoid straining—exhale on bowel movements.
- Sleep/recovery: Flexible training volume on low-sleep days; keep at least one mobility/breath-only session weekly. Consider brief high-waist supportive garments for comfort (not tight binders).

PROGRESSION AND COACHING NOTES
- Add only one variable at a time: reps, tempo, range, or load.
- Watch the midline for doming and monitor pelvic floor symptoms at all new steps.
- Keep core blocks short and high-quality (8–12 minutes), 2–3x/week.
- If any setbacks or symptoms, return to the last asymptomatic variation and consider referral to a pelvic health physical therapist.

This consolidated plan keeps her steadily progressing from restorative movement to moderate strength and optional light impact by Weeks 11–12, while aligning with OB guidance and postpartum best practices.
